mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate above 4.0% over the past month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede corporate earnings declines and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0% for one month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 4.0% and the unemployment rate rises above 4.0% in the same month, it signals a dual stress of monetary easing and labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 4.0 and UNRATE > 4.0.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1,300,000 units per month indicates weakening consumer demand for housing, which typically precedes a slowdown in overall economic activity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST falls below 1,300,000 units.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production above 104.0 index points indicates strengthening manufacturing output, which typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 104.0.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year increase in CPI above 2.5% signals rising inflation expectations, which typically prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL yoy growth exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales below 700,000 million dollars indicates weakening consumer spending, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS falls below 700,000 million.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls above 150,000 thousand persons indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 thousand.
